arjun: Heads up — saw a perf regression after the kernel-selector swap on canary. p95 up ~8-12% for mixes with many short (<=32) + long (>1024) sequences. Queue latency spikes and soft-429s increasing.
mel: Looking at profiler traces now. Kernel fallback path is hot, memory copies spiking around KV cache miss boundary. I’ll paste the hot stack.
mel: ```
hot: kernel_selector.cc:142
  memcpy_gpu -> kv_cache_lookup -> batch_assembler -> runtime_loop
  seq_var branches much more often than before
```
jj: This sounds like batching heuristics are mixing too many seq-lengths and forcing kernel switches. Two quick levers: 1) bias batch formation toward homogeneous seq-length groups when variance > X, 2) add admission preference for requests with KV cache hit probability to reduce overall token work.
lee: Can we detail the admission policy change? Are we talking hard reject, soft 429, or marking for lower-priority queue? I want to avoid oscillation.
arjun: Proposal: token-lease per-request window + KV-priority bump. Rough sketch: when a request enters, estimate expected_tokens. If admitted_tokens + expected_tokens > token_budget -> soft-429 (Shed). But if request has kv_hit_score >= 0.8, allow if admitted_tokens + expected_tokens <= token_budget + kv_slack. KV hits get small slack to favor cheap work.
sasha: Need metric hooks: admitted_kv_hit_ratio, token_budget_utilization, soft_429_rate_by_route, queue_wait_hist. I'll update the console dashboard if we pick metrics.
mel: I can run an experiment toggling homogeneous-batch-first heuristic. Config snippet I'm thinking:
mel: ```yaml
batching:
  homogeneous_threshold: 0.25   # if seq-length variance fraction > 0.25, form homogeneous batches
  max_batch_delay_ms: 12
admission:
  token_budget_window_ms: 1000
  token_budget_tokens: 20000
  kv_slack_tokens: 256
  soft_429_threshold_pct: 0.9
```

jj: For safe rollout, start canary: enable homogeneous batching + kv_slack=128, log admit decision details and compute expected cost delta. No hard 429s initially — only soft-429 metric and synthetic client retries.
infra-bot: deploybot: kernel-selector v2 rolled to canary (canary cluster: r-infer-canary-3) at 2026-03-17T16:02:03Z
lee: Also think about slow-start scale-down instead of immediate hard rejection. If budget exceeded, we can progressively reduce batch size and increase max_batch_delay to absorb spikes.
arjun: Agree. Step plan:
1) mel toggles homogeneous batch heuristic on canary + enable admit logging (today)
2) jj enables KV-priority admit slack=128 and soft_429 logging (tomorrow)
3) Collect 48h of metrics: p50/p95 latency, admitted_kv_hit_ratio, soft_429_rate, kernel_switch_rate (new metric)
4) If p95 improves or kernel_switch_rate drops >15% without increasing soft_429s > 2x, roll to 10% prod

sasha: Who owns the dashboards and alert thresholds? I can add temp alerts: soft_429_rate > 1% over baseline -> paging, kernel_switch_rate delta > 10% -> warn.
mel: Running the first run now. I'll attach small log sample in 15m.
arjun: Thanks — key asks: keep decision logs lightweight (one-line per request id), and include estimated_tokens, kv_score, admitted_bucket, reason. Example:
arjun: ```
req=xyz123 est_tokens=42 kv_score=0.92 admit=allow kv_slack_used=32 reason=kv_priority
req=xyz124 est_tokens=2048 kv_score=0.10 admit=soft_429 reason=budget_exceeded
```

jj: Also add a flag to opt-in per-model: some models are cheap and should get higher kv_slack, others not. We should store per-model token_cost_estimate.
lee: I'll prepare the experiment config PR for runtime. Tagging @mel @jj for review.
mel: PR up in 10m. Will also add a short perf test that forces mixed-seq batches to validate kernel-switch metric.
arjun: Great. If anyone sees client errors spike, ping here immediately. :thumbsup:
